stories.groq_explain: Hardened C++26 libraries add runtime checks to catch programming errors that would otherwise cause undefined behavior, like out-of-bounds access. Instead of crashing unpredictably or corrupting memory, these checks terminate the program safely when a violation occurs. It’s a way to make C++ safer without changing how most code works, just making errors more visible and controlled.
